title: bug: VS Code Plan Review and Task Detail show a step's original description instead of its active amendment, yet Approve sends the amended planRevision, so a human approves step text they never saw (VS Code twin of the DONE JetBrains fix 37e03b91)
description:
Filed by defect hunt 11-03 #5 (task-b7332618). VS Code twin of task-37e03b91, which JetBrains fixed in 3b56ee35. PROBLEM moe.amend_plan_step never rewrites a step's `description`. - It appends {amendmentId, description, reason, amendedBy, amendedAt} to `step.amendments` and points `step.activeAmendmentId` at the new entry (packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/amendPlanStep.ts:107-110). - It is allowed in every status except DONE and ARCHIVED (:71-73), so AWAITING_APPROVAL is included. - The approval surface holds the effective text: taskStore.ts:132-140, `effectiveDescription: effectiveStepDescription(step)`. - So an amendment bumps planRevision (derivePlanRevision, taskStore.ts:172-199), and Approve binds to the amended revision. Every VS Code renderer prints only `step.description`: - moe-vscode/src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts:742, renderSteps: the initial Plan Review HTML, which Approve is clicked on. - moe-vscode/media/planReview.js:168, renderSteps: the live update. - moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts:1146, renderSteps. - moe-vscode/media/taskDetail.js:369, renderSteps: the live update. moe-vscode/src/types/moe.ts:162-171 (ImplementationStep) has no amendments or activeAmendmentId field. Nothing under moe-vscode/src or moe-vscode/media mentions "amend". EVIDENCE Repro on 19d5e67a (the moe/work-2026-10-24 tip; it includes 585fedc6), run in a git-archive snapshot outside the checkout. The re-run recipe is /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-b733/notes.md. cp /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-b733/zz-hunt-b733-steps.test.cjs $S/moe-vscode/tests/ cd $S/moe-vscode && NODE_PATH=/mnt/d/projexts/moes/moe-vscode/node_modules node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/zz-hunt-b733-steps.test.cjs The test runs the production renderers on a step whose active amendment reads "AMENDED: edit src/a.ts and delete src/b.ts". Result: `# fail 4` (steps.output.txt): - A1, PlanReviewPanel.renderSteps:
ORIGINAL: edit src/a.ts only
- A2, planReview.js: Step 1: PENDING ORIGINAL: edit src/a.ts only Affected files: src/a.ts - A3, TaskDetailPanel.renderSteps:
ORIGINAL: edit src/a.ts only
- A4, taskDetail.js: ○ Step 1: PENDING ORIGINAL: edit src/a.ts only Files: src/a.ts FIX DIRECTION Mirror the daemon's one resolution rule, packages/moe-daemon/src/util/planAmendments.ts activeAmendment / effectiveStepDescription. The same rule is in JetBrains ImplementationStep.effectiveDescription (3b56ee35). - Use the entry `activeAmendmentId` names, never simply the latest. - Fall back to the original description when the id is blank or dangling, when `amendments` is not an array, or when the entry has no string description. - Render that text in all four places, with a short "Amended by " marker. Keep the original reachable, for example as a title tooltip. - Add the optional fields to ImplementationStep in types/moe.ts. - Step text goes through escapeHtml on the TS side and textContent in the webview scripts; never innerHTML (a forbidden pattern). FILES - moe-vscode/src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts - moe-vscode/media/planReview.js - moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts (renderSteps only; its 'prev'/'next' message case belongs to the sibling hunt row for the WORKING left arrow) - moe-vscode/media/taskDetail.js - moe-vscode/src/types/moe.ts - one new moe-vscode/tests/*.test.cjs The hunt repro shows how to load each renderer (transpiled panels; raw webview scripts under node:vm). Related, not a duplicate: task-c5c092ae is the same bug class in the moe-compaction-keeper mod. The gate snapshot must be the full tree: mem:gotcha-vscode-tests-need-full-repo-snapshot.
definitionOfDone: Plan Review (PlanReviewPanel.ts initial HTML and media/planReview.js live render) and Task Detail (TaskDetailPanel.ts initial HTML and media/taskDetail.js live render) show the active amendment's description for a step whose activeAmendmentId names an entry in amendments, with an "Amended by <amendedBy>" marker. A step with no activeAmendmentId, or a blank or dangling one, shows its original description and no marker.

A new moe-vscode node test runs the production renderers (PlanReviewPanel.ts and TaskDetailPanel.ts transpiled; media/planReview.js and media/taskDetail.js raw under node:vm) on amended, unamended and dangling-id steps. It passes on the fix, and its amended-step cases fail when the four renderers are restored to the merge-base.
`npm ci && npm test && npm run compile` passes in moe-vscode in a full-repo git-archive snapshot outside the checkout.

implementationPlan.description:
RED tests first. Create moe-vscode/tests/step-amendment.test.cjs with the Write tool, byte for byte from the reference /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-e9a25fbf/step-amendment.test.cjs (sha256 e4dcc63f24073bf4a641c492ffc560a361e0293a7cb9931fb559bb8fccd5fbd3). Rail: tracked files are written only through Edit/Write, never cp or git apply.

What the test pins (mem:convention-vscode-renderer-tests). It loads the REAL renderers:
- PlanReviewPanel.ts and TaskDetailPanel.ts, transpiled with ts.transpileModule into node:vm. It calls their private renderSteps through `Panel.prototype.renderSteps.call({}, steps)`.
- media/planReview.js and media/taskDetail.js, raw under node:vm with a small DOM stand-in. It calls their top-level renderSteps.

There are 10 cases x 4 renderers = 40 rows, named `<case> <renderer>: ...`. The renderer is one of plan-review-html, plan-review-live, task-detail-html or task-detail-live.
- A1: the entry activeAmendmentId names is shown, not the latest one.
- A2: a blank amendedBy reads 'Amended by unknown'.
- A3: hostile amendment, amender and original text stays text.
- A4: malformed entries before the named one are skipped, and a non-string amendedBy reads unknown.
- O1 never amended; O2 dangling id; O3 blank id; O4 amendments not an array; O5 the named entry's description is not a string; O6 non-string id. Each shows the original description and no marker.

Step 4's RED re-proof counts the A-row ids, so do not rename the cases or the renderer labels.

Quick test run from the worktree root. The worktree has no node_modules, so read the control checkout's TS6 JS typescript, read-only:
`cd moe-vscode && NODE_PATH=/mnt/d/projexts/moes/moe-vscode/node_modules node --test --test-reporter=tap tests/step-amendment.test.cjs`
It must be RED now: `# fail 16` (exactly the A-rows) and `# pass 24`.

Shared rule and the two HTML renderers: moe-vscode/src/types/moe.ts, moe-vscode/src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts and moe-vscode/src/panels/TaskDetailPanel.ts. Copy these three files' hunks from /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-e9a25fbf/fix.diff with Edit. The diff's sha256 is 94488338b7bea88f673077e48aa1835388f59121ad6f9d22dfc3653da8a88012, and `git apply --check` passes against 6d6bdc51. (a) moe.ts: - Above ImplementationStep (line 162), add `export interface StepAmendment { amendmentId: string; description: string; reason?: string; amendedBy?: string; amendedAt?: string; }`, with a one-line doc comment naming packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts StepAmendment. - Add optional `amendments?: StepAmendment[]` and `activeAmendmentId?: string` to ImplementationStep, each with a short doc comment. (b) PlanReviewPanel.ts: - Add ImplementationStep and StepAmendment to the existing `import type` line. - Below escapeHtml (line 856), add two exported module functions, both with doc comments: - `activeStepAmendment(step)` returns the `step.amendments` entry whose amendmentId equals `step.activeAmendmentId` and whose description is a string. It returns null when the id is not a non-empty string or amendments is not an array. It never throws and never falls back to the latest entry. Doc comment: it mirrors activeAmendment in packages/moe-daemon/src/util/planAmendments.ts, and media/planReview.js and media/taskDetail.js carry the same rule. - `stepTextHtml(step)`. With no amendment it returns exactly today's `
${escapeHtml(step.description)}
`. With one it returns `
${escapeHtml(amendment.description)}
` followed by `
Amended by ${escapeHtml(by)}
`. Here `by` is amendedBy when it is a string whose trim() is non-blank, else 'unknown'. Keep that markup order (class first, then title), because the test reads it with a regex. - renderSteps (line 720) takes `steps: ImplementationStep[]`, and its description line becomes `${stepTextHtml(step)}`. Keep renderSteps a prototype method that never touches `this`: the test calls it on an empty receiver. - In the panel's style block, add `.step-amended { margin-top: 4px; font-size: 11px; font-style: italic; color: var(--vscode-descriptionForeground); }` right after the `.step-description` rule. (c) TaskDetailPanel.ts: - Add stepTextHtml to the existing `./PlanReviewPanel` import (line 3), and ImplementationStep to its `import type` list. - renderSteps (line 1125) takes `ImplementationStep[]` and uses `${stepTextHtml(step)}` for its description line. - Add the same `.step-amended` rule after its `.step-description` rule. - Do not touch its 'prev'/'next' message case; task-3ab5be0d owns it. Error handling: both renderSteps run while the panel builds its whole HTML, so a throw here blanks Plan Review or Task Detail. .moe/tasks is hand-editable. That is why activeStepAmendment checks typeof and Array.isArray before reading anything and returns null rather than throwing, and why a non-string amendedBy is never trimmed. A step that was never amended keeps exactly today's markup. Run step 1's quick test command: the 8 *-html A-rows turn green, and only the 8 *-live A-rows still fail.

Live renderers and the changelog: moe-vscode/media/planReview.js, moe-vscode/media/taskDetail.js and moe-vscode/CHANGELOG.md. Copy them with Edit from the same fix.diff hunks.

(a) In each script, add a top-level `function activeStepAmendment(step)` directly above `function renderSteps(steps)` (planReview.js line 137, taskDetail.js line 331).
- Same rule as the TS helper, as a plain ES5 loop: a non-empty string id, Array.isArray(step.amendments), and an object entry with a string description and a matching amendmentId; else null.
- Give it a 4-line comment naming src/panels/PlanReviewPanel.ts and the daemon's planAmendments.ts.

(b) In each renderSteps, replace the description block (planReview.js lines 166-169, taskDetail.js lines 367-370):
- `var amendment = activeStepAmendment(step);`
- desc.textContent is `amendment ? amendment.description : (step.description || '')`.
- When there is an amendment, append a div with className 'step-amended'. Its textContent is 'Amended by ' + (amendedBy when it is a string whose trim() is non-blank, else 'unknown'), and its title is 'Original step: ' + (step.description || '').
- Set text only through textContent and title, never through the markup-injection DOM property (a project.json globalRails.forbiddenPatterns entry).

(c) Do not touch planReview.js applyRenderedTask/tokenForTask or taskDetail.js renderedPlanRevision. Approval latching is unchanged; only the step text block changes.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: Every VS Code renderer of a plan step shows the step's active amendment text: the entry `activeAmendmentId` names in `amendments`, never simply the latest. The four renderers are the Plan Review HTML (PlanReviewPanel.renderSteps), its live update (media/planReview.js renderSteps), the Task Detail HTML (TaskDetailPanel.renderSteps) and its live update (media/taskDetail.js renderSteps). The text is followed by an 'Amended by <amendedBy>' line whose title tooltip is 'Original step: <original>'. This is the text the daemon's plan revision covers, and so the text Approve binds to (packages/moe-daemon/src/util/planAmendments.ts, taskStore.ts approvalPlanSurface). A step with no usable amendment renders exactly as before: its own description and no marker. 'No usable amendment' means a missing, blank, non-string or dangling id; non-array amendments; or a named entry whose description is not a string.
acceptanceCriteria: A step with amendments [amend-1, amend-2] and activeAmendmentId 'amend-1' renders amend-1's description as its .step-description text. It also gets a .step-amended element with the text 'Amended by <amendedBy>' and the title 'Original step: <original description>', in all four renderers.
An amendedBy that is missing, blank or not a string renders 'Amended by unknown'.
Step, amendment and amender text is escaped with escapeHtml in the panel HTML, and set through textContent/title in the webviews. An `` in an amendment never reaches the HTML as a tag.
These steps render the original description and no marker: no amendments, a dangling id, a blank id, a non-string id, non-array amendments, and a named entry whose description is not a string.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) The extension host adds an effectiveDescription to each step before posting updateTask. Rejected: it changes the payload both webviews and the approval-token code read, and the HTML render would still need the rule. (2) A new src/util module for the TS helper. Rejected: it adds a file, and TaskDetailPanel already imports shared helpers from PlanReviewPanel (seedRevisionAttribute, showApprovalRefusal). (3) The webviews cannot import TS, so each carries a 10-line ES5 copy of the rule, pinned by the same 40 test rows across all four renderers. Chosen.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: planReview.js applyRenderedTask re-renders the steps on every updateTask and latches Approve off when the revision changed, which an amendment does. The human then reopens the panel, and the reopened HTML comes from PlanReviewPanel.renderSteps, which shows the original text while Approve is armed on the amended revision. taskDetail.js re-renders the steps and then arms renderedPlanRevision with no latch, so Task Detail's Approve binds the amended revision while it shows the original text. The JetBrains fix 3b56ee35 is the parity reference.

- Backslash-u escapes typed into an Edit become literal characters (the taskDetail.js step icons). Keep those lines out of edits and check the non-ASCII counts.
- A non-string amendedBy must not reach .trim().
- task-3ab5be0d edits TaskDetailPanel.ts's prev/next message case, a different hunk. Do not touch it.
